summary: [¶] Petition under Section 79(1)(c), 79(1)(h) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 15 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 1999, Regulations 42 and 44 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and Generation Network Access to the Inter-State Transmission System) Regulations, 2022 and Regulations 57 and 68 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Indian Electricity Grid Code) Regulations, 2023 seeking relaxation of Regulation 22(3)(c) of the Indian Electricity Grid Code, 2023 for permitting commissioning of the Wind Turbine Generators (WTGs) in tranches of at least 5 MW for the Petitioner’s Wind Power Project. [¶] Continuum Power Trading (TN) Pvt. Ltd. has filed the Petition under Section 79(1)(c), 79(1)(h) and 79(1)(i) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulations 57 and 58 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Indian Electricity Grid Code) Regulations, 2023 and Regulations 41 and 42 of the CERC (Connectivity and General Network Access to the Inter-State Transmission System) Regulations, 2022 seeking relaxation of Regulation 22(3)(c) of the IEGC, 2023 to permit phase-wise commissioning/ trial run of its 36 MW ISTS-connected Wind Power Project at Meghpar, Kutch, Gujarat in tranches of not less than 5 MW, on account of delayed grant of connectivity, deferred connectivity start date of 19.11.2026 and resultant impediment in commissioning technically ready project capacity. [para 10] 10. The Project has reached an advanced stage of construction with land acquisition completed, the evacuation substation functional, the augmentation transformer installed, and multiple WTGs installed. As on date, the Petitioner is in a position to commission 21 MW out of the total 36 MW capacity. Regulation 22(3)(c) of the IEGC, 2023 requires a trial run for a minimum aggregate capacity. Strict application of the provision is preventing 21 MW of ready green energy from reaching the grid and is operating as a practical impediment to phased commissioning. The Petitioner intends to sell power through the Power Exchange and submits that phased commissioning in tranches of not less than 5 MW would align commissioning with actual project readiness, prevent continued stranding of ready generation capacity, and would not compromise grid security or operational reliability. [para 11] 11. The Petitioner submits that failure to commission by 30.06.2026 would result in the loss of the benefit of a 75% ISTS charges waiver. The impediments have arisen solely on account of the delayed grant of connectivity, the non-availability of transmission infrastructure and the resultant regulatory constraints beyond the Petitioner's control. Accordingly, the Petitioner has sought relaxation of Regulation 22(3)(c) of the IEGC, 2023 to permit phase-wise trial run and commissioning of its 36 MW Wind Power Project in tranches of not less than 5 MW and consequential directions for implementation of such phased commissioning. [para 20] 20. We are unable to agree with the Petitioner’s argument that it would have completed the project in 7 months had it been issued the in-principle grant of connectivity in August 2024, when it could not complete the project in 18 months. Also, the Petitioner cannot claim that it must be given Connectivity for 7 months as per its requirement.
